title: Valid Parenthesis String
prompt:
Given a string `s` of `(`, `)`, and `*`, return whether it can be valid. Each `*` may be treated as `(`, `)`, or an empty string. Valid means every `(` has a matching `)` after it, and vice versa.

**Example**: `"(*)"` → `true`; `"(*))"` → `true`; `")("` → `false`.

**Constraints**: `1 ≤ s.length ≤ 100`.
hints: Trying all 3 meanings of every `*` is exponential. Instead of one open-paren count, could you track every count that is still possible?
The possible counts form a contiguous range `[low, high]`: `(` raises both, `)` lowers both, and `*` lowers `low` (acts as `)`) while raising `high` (acts as `(`).
If `high < 0`, return false. Clamp `low` at 0 after each char. At the end, return `low == 0`.

solution.explanation: `[low, high]` is exactly the set of open counts some assignment of the stars can produce so far. If `high < 0`, even the most generous choice has an unmatched `)`. Clamping `low` at 0 drops choices that would go negative. If 0 is still possible at the end, some assignment balances. O(n) time, O(1) space.
